caption: United States v. Gwinnett
citation_line: United States v. Gwinnett, 483 F.3d 200 (3d Cir. 2007)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Hayden accepted a Rule 11(c)(1)(C) plea containing mutual appellate waivers and imposed the agreed 30-month sentence for mail fraud and tax evasion.
qualification_rationale: The appeal resolved an important recurring question about the legal effect of criminal appellate waivers and corrected loose jurisdictional terminology in earlier circuit decisions.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit affirmed in a precedential opinion. It held that an appellate waiver does not divest the court of subject-matter jurisdiction, but a knowing and voluntary waiver will be enforced absent a miscarriage of justice.
